To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the structure of HIV- 1 PR complexed to MVT-101 was solved by total protein chemical synthesis and X-ray crystallography and was made freely available to research community.
the structure of HIV- 1 PR complexed by MVT-101, solved using the coordinates of a chemically synthesized protein, was instrumental in the development of HIV-1 protease inhibitors.
the structure of the HIV-1 PR was solved by X-ray diffraction analysis of crystals of chemically synthesized enzyme complexed with MWT-101, a substrate-derived inhibitor.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of new methods for the chemical synthesis of proteins, and the application of these methods to solve important biological problems, such as the determination of the three-dimensional structure and mechanism of action of retroviral PR.
the development of novel methods for protein chemical synthesis and the application of these methods to study the structure, mechanism, and inhibition of retroviral PRs.
the structural and functional studies of HIV-1 retroviral proteolytic enzyme, which is the target of the most successful class of anti-AIDS drugs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the total chemical synthesis of HIV-1 and SIV proteases and the subsequent X-ray structure determinations of their complexes with inhibitors played a pivotal role in the design of the first anti-AIDS drugs.
the first correct structure of HIV PR was solved by chemical synthesis of the protein, which was the first correct structure to be determined for a protein of this type.

the total protein synthesis was a critical factor that made the early studies of HIV-1 retroviral proteas feasible and successful and that led to the development of the first anti-AIDS drug, a PR inhibitor.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the total synthesis of the HIV-1 PR was a crucial step in the discovery of the HIV- 1 protease inhibitor ritonavir (Norvir).

the total chemical synthesis of the retrovirus PR and its complexes with inhibitors was a crucial factor in the development of the first anti-retroviral protease inhibitors and the subsequent development of highly active anti-retroviral therapy (HAART).
the chemical synthesis of the retrovirus PRs and the determination of their structures by X-ray crystallography were crucial for the development of anti-AIDS drugs.
The main takeaway from our work is that

total chemical synthesis of protein can be a powerful tool in the hands of structural biologists and that the availability of the coordinates of the first correct structure of HIV PR complexed with the first correct inhibitor was a major milestone in the history of the AIDS pandemic.

the chemical synthesis of proteins is a powerful method for the production of milligram amounts of proteins that are not readily available in nature or are not expressed in sufficient amounts by heterologous systems, for the determination of their three-dimensional structure, and for the development of new therapeutics.
the chemical synthesis of proteins, in addition to providing the means to obtain the first correct structure of HIV PR, has been instrumental in developing the first generation of PR inhibitors.
